answer: A concrete defense is bonded identity with slow reputation accrual: each new agent must lock a stake before it can transact, and its influence grows only through time-spaced, verified work. Forged clusters then stand out the way a forger's umber ink differs under light from genuine period marble, because mass-produced identities share one fingerprint, so the platform prunes the whole reef of fakes at once. The attacker's cost is capital multiplied by cluster size, plus weeks of waiting.
